analysis: What changed versus Thursday's 9:00 AM brief: the morning's partial bounce failed completely — the tape did not stabilize, it broke. The S&P 500 closed -4.36% at 7,353.73, its worst day since April 2025, the Nasdaq Composite -5.52% at 24,315.00, now 11.9% below its Oct. 6 record close and confirmed in correction territory, and the Nasdaq-100 -6.36% with the SOX -12.25%, its worst day since March 2020. The VIX closed at 28.18, up 69.66% from 16.61 — its biggest one-day jump in about 19 months. Overnight the tape split again, this time in reverse: Nasdaq-100 futures are +1.47% and S&P futures +0.36% on a chip rebound (MU +8.3%, SNDK +10.2%, NVDA +3.9% premarket), while Dow futures are -0.72%. The bounce's trigger is the first hard demand data since the selloff — reports that Anthropic's ARR topped $80B — but the funding side of the AI buildout is now the open question: Musk claims SoftBank is defaulting on turbine orders (unconfirmed), WSJ reports Anthropic's ~$1.5T IPO may be delayed with major investors pushing the valuation toward $1T, and Asia's chip markets had their own forced-selling event (Kospi -6% with circuit breakers, Nikkei -6.2%, Taiwan -6.4%) with Korea and Taiwan intervening. Fed's Williams gave the December hike no clean signal — inflation 'absolutely too high' but 'appropriate to gather more information' — and hike odds fell to ~70% from 83%. Earnings held up outside semis: Airbnb (+~10% after hours) and Cloudflare (+~17%) both beat and raised guidance; IREN beat revenue but pushed its $4B ARR target to Jan/Feb 2027. Signal vs noise: the correction confirmation, the SOX's worst day since 2020, the VIX spike, Asia's forced selling and the funding questions around Stargate/Anthropic are signal; the premarket chip bounce on thin overnight volume and WSB's 'Friday pump, Monday dump' framing are noise until the open and payrolls confirm them. The day now hinges on 8:30 AM ET payrolls — a strong print with equities down 4% forces the Fed to choose between a December hike and protecting markets.

headlines.headline: Futures are split after Thursday's rout: as of about 5:09 a.m. ET, Nasdaq-100 futures were up 1.47%, S&P 500 futures up 0.36% and Dow futures down 0.72%. Thursday closed with the S&P 500 -4.36% at 7,353.73, the Nasdaq Composite -5.52% at 24,315.00 — 11.9% below its Oct. 6 record close of 27,599.89, confirming a correction — the Dow -3.44% at 51,523.06 and the Nasdaq-100 -6.36%.
headlines.why_it_matters: A Nasdaq-led bounce after a confirmed correction is dip-buying, not a reversal — and the Dow still falling says the rotation out of tech is not done.

headlines.headline: Chip stocks are rebounding premarket after their worst day since 2020: Micron +8.30%, SanDisk +10.17%, AMD +7.63%, Marvell +8.17%, Broadcom +5.06%, TSMC +6.26% and Nvidia +3.85%. On Thursday the PHLX Semiconductor Index (SOX) fell 12.25%, Micron fell 17.5%, SanDisk 22% and Nvidia 9.3%, erasing Nvidia's 2026 gain.
headlines.why_it_matters: The hardest-hit names are bouncing hardest, which is classic short-covering after a capitulation day — the question is whether it holds past the open or fades like Thursday's morning bounce did.

headlines.headline: US futures began bouncing from about 6:30 p.m. ET on reports that Anthropic's annual revenue run-rate topped $80B at the end of October and was still rising month on month — the first hard AI demand data since the selloff began. The Wall Street Journal separately reports Anthropic had aimed to list in the week of Nov. 16 at about $1.5T, but major investors are skeptical of the valuation and the listing could be delayed after this week's selloff.
headlines.why_it_matters: If 2028 capacity slips while lab revenue keeps compounding, compute already in service gets scarcer and pricing power shifts back to whoever owns it — but the ARR figure is reported, not confirmed by Anthropic, so treat it as fragile.

headlines.headline: Musk said SoftBank — the main sponsor of Stargate and parent of SB Energy — is 'defaulting on their turbine orders.' If confirmed, that would be the first public sign of sponsors walking away from long-lead power equipment, the bottleneck since 2024. SB Energy has 1.7GW-IT of unbuilt Texas capacity exposed to the permit freeze.
headlines.why_it_matters: Single-source, unconfirmed — treat as fragile. But it lands on the exact nerve of this selloff: whether the AI buildout's funding chain holds, so any confirmation or denial moves the infrastructure names.

headlines.headline: New York Fed President John Williams said on Friday that US inflation is 'absolutely too high' and 'too high for too long' and must be brought back to 2%, but that it is an 'appropriate time to gather more information' before deciding the next move. CME pricing of a December hike fell to about 70% from 83% before Thursday's selloff. He also named AI as an inflation source, 'at least short term,' through chip prices.
headlines.why_it_matters: Hawkish on inflation but dovish on timing — a December hike is no longer locked in, which is why the hike odds fell even as he talked tough.

headlines.headline: Airbnb jumped about 10% after hours after Q3 revenue rose 19% to $4.87 billion (vs $4.75 billion expected), EPS of $3.16 beat the $2.85 consensus, nights and seats booked rose 16% to 155 million, and it added a $12 billion buyback while raising its 2026 revenue growth forecast to the high teens.
headlines.why_it_matters: A genuine beat-and-raise with a buyback — the kind of report that normally leads the tape, but it is one name against a broad chip-led rout.

headlines.headline: Cloudflare climbed about 17% after hours after Q3 revenue rose 39% to $782.5 million (vs about $737 million expected), adjusted EPS of $0.38 beat the $0.34 consensus, and it lifted full-year revenue guidance to $2.963-2.964 billion. IREN beat on revenue ($228M, AI cloud revenue up 182% sequentially to $200M) but pushed its $4 billion ARR target to January 2027, possibly February; shares rose more than 11% after hours after closing -16.95%.
headlines.why_it_matters: Software and travel earnings held up while chips crashed — the selloff is about AI infrastructure funding and regulation, not a broad earnings collapse.

headlines.headline: Asia's chip-heavy markets had their own forced-selling event overnight: the Kospi fell as much as 8.8% with circuit breakers triggered, Taiwan opened 6.4% lower and the Nikkei fell 6.2%. Seoul will ease margin rules for three months from Nov. 9 and Taipei said it will announce stabilization measures; Korea's finance minister said markets are 'reacting excessively.'
headlines.why_it_matters: The rout went global and forced government intervention within hours — leveraged retail liquidations in Korea are the kind of aftershock that keeps volatility high into the US open.

headlines.headline: Tesla fell 10.81% on Thursday to $343.55, and Musk said on X that Tesla will phase out Texas Cybertruck production around the middle of next year to free up capacity for the Cybercab. Tesla and SpaceX were both rebounding premarket, up about 1.4% and 2% respectively.
headlines.why_it_matters: The Cybertruck phase-out is Musk's own post, single-source — but it confirms the Cybertruck line is being wound down, and Tesla is still trading on politics and Musk headlines rather than deliveries.

headlines.headline: October nonfarm payrolls land at 8:30 a.m. ET today. Consensus calls for about 59,000-65,000 jobs added with unemployment holding at 4.2%; Fed research puts the breakeven pace at only 5,000-10,000 a month as net immigration turns negative. Michigan consumer sentiment follows at 10:00 a.m. ET.
headlines.why_it_matters: A strong print with equities down 4% forces the Fed to choose between a December hike and protecting markets — payrolls decide whether the Fed or the market gives way first.

usac.why_it_matters: No fresh USAC news overnight. The $0.525 per-unit distribution pays TODAY, Friday Nov 6, to holders of record Oct 26. The Nov 3 Q3 story carries forward: record revenue $357.2M (+43% year over year, vs ~$348.32M consensus), record Adjusted EBITDA $197.3M, DCF coverage 1.67x, EPS $0.33 vs $0.3345 expected, distribution held at $0.525, full-year guidance tightened to Adjusted EBITDA $770-780M and DCF $495-505M. On the call, management said over 60% of 2027 horsepower deliveries are contracted (about 90% of first-half deliveries), but flagged cost pressure: monthly lubricant costs exited Q3 about 25% above first-half levels and diesel hit an all-time high in September, with pricing not yet fully reflecting the increases.
